merge rule: any deny among baseline and readings is returned immediately, an unaccepted baseline ask is kept, otherwise the strictest reading wins, and a non-exhaustive set whose strictest result is not an ask falls through to a too-complex outcome
write-path caller: builds the reading set, records incompleteness with ut||=!an, then re-decides once per reading and adopts any reading that denies
permission wrapper: collects names and operands, builds the reading set, re-decides per reading and merges with DTr(b,z,M); the range spans its definition to the readings call

implementation.portedInvariant: every reading the shell could run must satisfy a command rule, and an incomplete reading set may not be allowed on the strength of one reading
ownedDecisions: Readings come from this runtime's own shell model - de-quoting and unescaping, per-segment splitting on ; && || | and newline, and the bodies of command substitutions, each applied one level further - which is a conservative superset, so permission is never widened.

Incompleteness is decided by construct rather than by a parse: substitution, parameter expansion, process substitution, a locale-translated string, an unquoted variable, a leading tilde and a glob all make the set incomplete. The bound is 16 readings.
The recovered merge keeps the strictest reading through an ordering this runtime does not port; only the two rules carrying the safety property are kept.

Where the recovered merge falls through to a too-complex outcome an outer layer prompts on, this runtime returns an ask because it has no pass-through layer; it applies only when the decision would otherwise have been an allow, and never in bypass mode.
implementation.unchanged: A rule without a command constraint, a path-only rule, a non-shell tool, a baseline denial and bypass mode all behave exactly as before.

regressions: The full suite covers the permission, agent, skill and integration paths this touches; no previously passing case changed and only the four new cases were added.
limitations: The reading model is a conservative superset built from this runtime's own rules, not an enumeration derived from a shell grammar, so it can over-approximate what the shell would run and ask more often than the recovered analyser.
The recovered strictness ordering and its bashMissKind vocabulary are not ported, so a reading set whose strictest member is not a denial is resolved by the two safety rules alone.
Verified against owned fixtures and a loopback gateway, not against a real shell under adversarial input.
